companies.name: Acacia Communications
companies.description: Maker of coherent optical modules and DSP chips for data center and network links; acquired by Cisco in 2021.
companies.explain: Acacia's optics move data over fiber between data centers. Cisco paid about $4.5 billion for it after raising its first offer.

companies.name: American Electric Power
companies.description: One of the largest U.S. utilities, with transmission and distribution across 11 states including Ohio and Texas.
companies.explain: AEP serves many new data centers in Ohio and Texas and has committed billions to buy Bloom Energy fuel cells to power data centers while its grid is expanded.

companies.name: Alchip Technologies
companies.description: Taiwanese design-services firm that turns customers' AI chip designs into chips made at TSMC.
companies.explain: Alchip helps big tech companies finish and manufacture their own custom AI chips (ASICs), making it a quieter beneficiary of the custom-chip boom.

companies.name: Aligned Data Centers
companies.description: Private developer of hyperscale and AI data center campuses in the Americas.
companies.explain: Aligned builds and leases large, power-dense data centers to cloud and AI companies. In 2025 the AI Infrastructure Partnership, an investor group including BlackRock's GIP and MGX, agreed to buy it.

companies.name: Alphawave IP Group
companies.description: Designer of high-speed connectivity IP, chiplets and custom silicon for data centers; part of Qualcomm since December 2025.
companies.explain: Qualcomm bought Alphawave for $2.3B to get the high-speed connection technology it needs for data-center AI chips.

companies.name: Amazon (AWS)

source.quote: For contracts with original terms that exceed one year, those commitments not yet recognized were approximately $496 billion as of June 30, 2026.

companies.description: Online retailer whose Amazon Web Services (AWS) unit is the world's largest cloud provider and Anthropic's main cloud partner.
companies.explain: AWS rents out computing power, including its own Trainium AI chips. Anthropic and OpenAI have each committed more than $100 billion of future spending to AWS, most of Amazon's contracted backlog.

companies.name: AMD
companies.description: Designs CPUs and Instinct AI GPUs for data centers, PCs and game consoles.
companies.explain: AMD is the main alternative to Nvidia for AI GPUs. It has signed multi-gigawatt chip deals with OpenAI and Meta, paying them partly in AMD share warrants that vest as they buy.

companies.name: Amkor Technology
companies.description: Outsourced chip packaging and testing company; building a large advanced packaging plant in Arizona.
companies.explain: After chips are made on wafers they must be packaged and tested. Amkor does this for Apple, Nvidia and others, and its Arizona plant is key to making AI chips fully in the US.

companies.name: Ampere Computing
companies.description: Designs Arm-based server CPUs for cloud data centers; SoftBank agreed to buy it in 2025.
companies.explain: Ampere makes power-efficient Arm server chips. Oracle was a big early investor and customer; SoftBank agreed to buy the company in 2025 to support its AI chip plans.

companies.name: Amphenol
companies.description: Makes electrical and fiber optic connectors, cables and antennas, including high-speed interconnects for AI servers.
companies.explain: Amphenol makes the connectors and cables inside AI server racks. It paid $10.5 billion for CommScope's fiber connectivity business in 2025-26.

companies.name: Andreessen Horowitz
companies.description: Silicon Valley venture capital firm investing in AI labs and infrastructure startups.
companies.explain: a16z backs several new AI labs early, leading Thinking Machines Lab's $2 billion seed round and investing in xAI and Safe Superintelligence.

companies.name: Anthropic

source.quote: In 2023, 2024, and 2025, our revenue was $41 million, $386 million, and $4.6 billion, respectively, representing year-over-year growth rates of 841% and 1,088%, respectively.
Anthropic, an American AI company, has raised US$ 65 billion in a Series H funding round at a US$ 965 billion post-money valuation.

companies.description: Maker of the Claude AI models; a public benefit corporation that filed for a Nasdaq IPO in October 2026.
companies.explain: Anthropic is funded mainly by Amazon and Google, which are also its biggest cloud suppliers, so much of the money they invest flows back to them as computing spend.

companies.name: Anysphere (Cursor)

source.quote: The Exchange Ratio was calculated based on an implied equity value of Cursor of $60 billion and VWAP of the Company's Class A common stock over the seven consecutive trading days immediately preceding the closing of the Cursor Merger of $128.65.

companies.description: Maker of the Cursor AI coding editor; a SpaceX subsidiary since August 2026.
companies.explain: Cursor is one of the biggest buyers of AI model access (from OpenAI, Anthropic and others); SpaceX bought it in 2026 at a $60 billion value.

companies.name: Apollo Global Management

source.quote: Total AUM of $1.05 trillion benefited from inflows of $60 billion in the second quarter and $298 billion over the last twelve months

companies.description: Alternative asset manager and private credit lender that funds large industrial and chip-factory projects.
companies.explain: Apollo provides big private-credit and equity checks to capital-hungry tech builders, such as the $11 billion it led for a 49% stake in Intel's Fab 34 in Ireland.

companies.name: Apple
companies.description: Maker of the iPhone and Mac; builds Apple Intelligence features and licenses outside AI models.
companies.explain: Apple spends less on its own AI data centers than its peers and instead pays partners such as Google for AI models, making it a major customer rather than a builder.

companies.name: Applied Digital
companies.description: Builds and leases 'AI Factory' data center campuses, including Polaris Forge 1 in North Dakota leased to CoreWeave.
companies.explain: Applied Digital went from hosting crypto miners to building AI data centers. Long leases with CoreWeave and unnamed investment-grade hyperscalers make it a landlord for AI compute.

companies.name: Applied Materials
companies.description: Largest US maker of chipmaking equipment, covering deposition, etching, inspection and other wafer processing steps.
companies.explain: When chipmakers build new fabs for AI chips, a large share of the equipment budget goes to toolmakers like Applied Materials.

companies.name: Arista Networks
companies.description: Makes high-speed Ethernet switches and routers for cloud and AI data centers.
companies.explain: Arista sells the switches that connect servers and GPUs inside the biggest cloud and AI data centers. Microsoft and Meta alone buy roughly a third of its gear, so their AI spending flows straight into Arista's revenue.

companies.name: Arm Holdings
companies.description: Designs and licenses the Arm processor architecture used in most phones and a growing share of data-center chips.
companies.explain: Arm doesn't sell chips; it earns license fees and royalties when others (Apple, Nvidia, Amazon, Qualcomm) build chips on its designs. SoftBank owns most of it after Nvidia's $40B takeover failed.

companies.name: ASE Technology

source.quote: For the full year of 2025, the Company reported unaudited net revenues of NT$645,388 million and net income attributable to shareholders of the parent of NT$40,658 million.

companies.description: World's largest chip packaging and testing company (includes SPIL), also an electronics manufacturing services provider.
companies.explain: ASE packages and tests chips, including advanced packaging needed for AI processors. Revenue is unaudited NT$645.4 billion for 2025, converted by AI Atlas at about NT$31.4 per US dollar (approximate 2025 average).

companies.name: ASML

source.quote: ASML reported another record year in 2025, with total net sales of €32.7 billion and a gross margin of 52.8%.

companies.description: Dutch maker of lithography machines, the only supplier of the EUV tools needed to make the most advanced chips.
companies.explain: Every leading-edge chip factory (TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SK hynix) must buy ASML's EUV machines, which cost hundreds of millions of dollars each. Revenue is €32.7 billion for 2025, converted by AI Atlas at about $1.13 per euro (approximate 2025 average).

companies.name: Astera Labs
companies.description: Designs connectivity chips that link GPUs, CPUs and memory inside AI servers.
companies.explain: Astera Labs sells the small chips that keep data flowing between processors and memory inside AI servers, so it grows with every AI server shipped.

companies.name: BlackRock

source.quote: $15.5 trillion in AUM following $869 billion of net inflows over the last twelve months, representing 10% organic base fee growth

companies.description: World's largest asset manager; owns Global Infrastructure Partners and co-founded the AI Infrastructure Partnership with Microsoft, Nvidia and MGX.
companies.explain: Through its infrastructure arm GIP and the AI Infrastructure Partnership, BlackRock buys and funds data centers and power, including the roughly $40 billion purchase of Aligned Data Centers.

companies.name: Blackstone

source.quote: Total AUM increased to $1,368.3 billion, up 10% year-over-year, with $63.3 billion of inflows in the quarter and $271.6 billion over the LTM.

companies.description: World's largest alternative asset manager; owns data center developer QTS and lends to AI cloud companies.
companies.explain: Blackstone owns QTS, one of the biggest US data center builders, and led multi-billion-dollar GPU-backed loans to CoreWeave, so it earns from both AI buildings and AI chips.

companies.name: Bloom Energy
companies.description: Maker of solid oxide fuel cells that generate on-site electricity from natural gas or hydrogen.
companies.explain: Bloom's fuel cells let data centers get power on site without waiting for the grid; Oracle, AEP and CoreWeave have signed large deals with it.

companies.name: Blue Owl Capital

source.quote: With $319 billion in assets under management as of June 30, 2026, we invest across three multi-strategy platforms: Credit, Real Assets and GP Strategic Capital.

companies.description: Alternative asset manager that funds data center campuses through joint ventures and private credit.
companies.explain: Blue Owl's funds put up much of the money for giant AI campuses that others run, such as Meta's Hyperion site in Louisiana and Crusoe's Abilene, Texas campus.

companies.name: Boyd Thermal
companies.description: Maker of liquid cooling and thermal systems for data centers and aerospace; acquired by Eaton in 2026.
companies.explain: Boyd Thermal makes liquid cooling for hot AI chips. Eaton paid $9.5 billion for it.

companies.name: Broadcom
companies.description: Designs custom AI chips (like Google's TPUs) and the networking chips that connect AI data centers.
companies.explain: Broadcom builds custom AI chips for big buyers that want an alternative to Nvidia, including Google, Anthropic and OpenAI, and supplies much of the networking inside AI data centers.

companies.name: Brookfield Renewable
companies.description: Brookfield's listed renewable power arm, owning hydro, wind, solar and storage worldwide.
companies.explain: Brookfield Renewable signed record clean-power frameworks with Microsoft (10.5 GW) and Google (up to 3 GW of hydro, with $3B+ of initial contracts).

companies.name: Brookfield Asset Management

source.publisher: Brookfield Asset Management Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (SEC EDGAR)
source.quote: Brookfield Asset Management Ltd. (NYSE: BAM, TSX: BAM) is a leading global alternative asset manager, headquartered in New York, with over $1 trillion of assets under management across infrastructure, energy, private equity, real estate, and credit.

companies.description: Global alternative asset manager investing in infrastructure, power and real estate, including chip fabs and fuel-cell power.
companies.explain: Brookfield supplies long-term capital to AI's physical layer: it co-funds Intel's Arizona chip factories and set up a financing framework of up to $5 billion for Bloom Energy fuel cells that power data centers.

companies.name: Calpine

source.quote: Significant Transactions and Developments Acquisition of Calpine Corporation On January 7, 2026, we acquired 100% of the outstanding equity of Calpine for a purchase price of approximately $22 billion.

companies.description: Large U.S. natural gas and geothermal power producer, acquired by Constellation in January 2026.
companies.explain: Calpine's gas fleet and Geysers geothermal plants became part of Constellation in a deal valued at about $22B at closing, making Constellation the largest U.S. power producer.

companies.name: Celestial AI
companies.description: Designer of Photonic Fabric optical interconnects that link AI chips and memory using light; part of Marvell since 2026.
companies.explain: Marvell paid $3.25B upfront (up to $5.5B) for Celestial AI, betting that light-based links will be needed to connect ever-larger AI chip clusters.

companies.name: Celestica
companies.description: Contract manufacturer that designs and builds data center switches, servers and storage for cloud companies.
companies.explain: Celestica builds networking switches and AI server hardware to order for hyperscalers (the giant cloud companies), so part of their AI spending ends up as Celestica revenue.

companies.name: Cerebras
companies.description: Designs wafer-scale AI chips and systems, and sells fast AI inference as a cloud service.
companies.explain: Cerebras builds dinner-plate-sized AI chips. It went public in May 2026 after landing OpenAI as a customer for 750 MW of compute; before that most of its revenue came from Abu Dhabi's G42.

companies.name: Character.AI
companies.description: Chatbot app that lets users talk with customizable AI characters.
companies.explain: Character.AI licensed its technology to Google for a reported $2.7 billion in 2024, when its founders returned to Google.

companies.name: Ciena
companies.description: Makes optical networking equipment and software for telecoms, cloud companies and data center interconnect.
companies.explain: Ciena's optical gear connects data centers to each other. Cloud companies building AI campuses are now among its biggest customers.

companies.name: Cipher Mining
companies.description: Bitcoin miner turned AI data center developer (renamed Cipher Digital in 2026) with sites in Texas.
companies.explain: Cipher leases Texas data center campuses to Amazon Web Services and to Fluidstack, whose rent is partly backstopped by Google.

companies.name: Cisco
companies.description: Makes networking equipment, optics and security software for enterprises, telecoms and data centers.
companies.explain: Cisco is the largest traditional networking company. It sells switches, routers and optics into AI data centers and has bought optical companies such as Acacia to compete there.

companies.name: Cloud Light
companies.description: Maker of optical transceivers for data centers; acquired by Lumentum in 2023.
companies.explain: Cloud Light builds the optical modules that connect AI servers. Lumentum paid about $750 million for it.

companies.name: Coatue Management
companies.description: New York technology investment firm running hedge funds and growth-stage venture funds.
companies.explain: Coatue co-led Anthropic's $30 billion Series G and co-led its Series H, and has also lent to AI cloud companies such as CoreWeave.

companies.name: Cogentrix Energy
companies.description: Owner of about 5.5 GW of natural gas power plants in PJM, New England and Texas; owned by Quantum Capital Group funds.
companies.explain: Vistra agreed to buy Cogentrix for about $4.0B in January 2026 to add gas plants for growing demand, including from data centers.

companies.name: Cohere
companies.description: Toronto-based maker of AI models and tools for businesses and governments.
companies.explain: Cohere sells AI to enterprises rather than consumers and is one of Canada's main AI labs; chip makers Nvidia and AMD are among its backers.

companies.name: Coherent
companies.description: Makes lasers, optical transceivers and materials used in data center networks and industry.
companies.explain: Coherent makes the optical transceivers that connect AI servers over fiber. Nvidia agreed in 2026 to invest $2 billion in it and to buy billions of dollars of its products.

companies.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems
companies.description: MIT spin-out building the SPARC fusion demo machine and the planned ARC fusion power plant in Virginia.
companies.explain: Google signed to buy 200 MW from CFS's first fusion power plant and invested in the company; Nvidia joined its $863M 2025 round.

companies.name: CommScope Connectivity and Cable Solutions

source.quote: Anticipates CCS will generate sales and EBITDA margins of approximately $3.6 billion and 26% in 2025, respectively

companies.description: Fiber and copper cabling and connectivity business sold by CommScope to Amphenol in January 2026.
companies.explain: This business makes the fiber cabling used inside data centers. Amphenol paid CommScope $10.5 billion for it.

companies.name: Compass Datacenters
companies.description: Private builder of hyperscale data center campuses, owned by Brookfield and Ontario Teachers'.
companies.explain: Compass designs and builds large data center campuses for cloud companies, part of the landlord layer behind AI compute.

companies.name: Constellation Energy
companies.description: Largest U.S. nuclear plant owner; also owns Calpine's gas and geothermal fleet since January 2026.
companies.explain: Constellation is the go-to seller of 24/7 carbon-free nuclear power to tech giants: it is restarting Three Mile Island Unit 1 for Microsoft and signed a 20-year deal with Meta for its Clinton plant.

companies.name: CoolTera
companies.description: UK maker of coolant distribution units and piping for data center liquid cooling; acquired by Vertiv in 2023.
companies.explain: CoolTera's equipment feeds coolant to liquid-cooled AI racks. Vertiv bought it for an undisclosed price.

companies.name: Core Scientific
companies.description: Former bitcoin miner converting its sites into high-density AI data centers leased to CoreWeave and AMD.
companies.explain: Core Scientific is a landlord to CoreWeave (about 590 MW of 12-year contracts) and, from 2026, AMD. CoreWeave tried to buy it for about $9 billion in 2025, but shareholders voted no.

companies.name: CoreWeave

source.quote: Revenue backlog1 was approximately $104 billion as of June 30, 2026.

companies.description: The largest specialist AI cloud: rents out Nvidia GPU capacity to OpenAI, Microsoft, Meta and other AI developers.
companies.explain: CoreWeave sits in the middle of the AI money web: Nvidia sells it chips, owns its shares and even buys its spare capacity, while OpenAI, Meta and Microsoft have committed tens of billions to rent its GPUs. Much of its buildout is paid for with debt.

companies.name: Corning
companies.description: Makes optical fiber, cable and connectivity products, plus specialty glass such as iPhone cover glass.
companies.explain: Corning makes the optical fiber that carries data between AI servers. AI data centers need far more fiber than older ones, and Meta signed an up-to-$6 billion fiber deal with Corning in 2026.

companies.name: Credo Technology
companies.description: Designs high-speed connectivity chips and active electrical cables for data centers.
companies.explain: Credo's cables and chips carry data short distances between AI servers and switches, a fast-growing need as AI clusters get bigger.

companies.name: Crusoe

source.quote: Share: DENVER – September 17, 2026 – Crusoe, the industry’s first vertically-integrated AI infrastructure provider, today announced the initial closing of its anticipated $3.9 billion Series F funding round, at a $30.9 billion post-money valuation.

companies.description: Builds and powers large AI data centers (including Stargate's Abilene campus for Oracle) and runs its own GPU cloud.
companies.explain: Crusoe both builds giant data centers for others, such as the Abilene, Texas Stargate campus used by Oracle and OpenAI, and rents GPUs through Crusoe Cloud. Nvidia has invested in several of its funding rounds.

companies.name: CyrusOne

source.quote: (NASDAQ: CONE) (the “Company” or “CyrusOne”) today announced the completion of its acquisition by funds managed by KKR, a leading global investment firm, and Global Infrastructure Partners (“GIP”), one of the world’s leading infrastructure investors, in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $15 billion, including the assumption of debt (the “Transaction”).

companies.description: Data center developer and operator owned by KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners since 2022.
companies.explain: CyrusOne leases large data centers to cloud and AI companies. KKR and GIP bought it for about $15 billion including debt in 2022.

companies.name: d-Matrix
companies.description: Designs in-memory computing chips for AI inference in data centers.
companies.explain: d-Matrix builds inference chips that do math inside memory to save power, one of several startups chasing the market for running AI models.

companies.name: Dell Technologies
companies.description: Makes servers, storage, PCs and networking gear, including AI servers.
companies.explain: Dell is one of the largest builders of AI servers, selling Nvidia-based systems to companies such as xAI and CoreWeave.

companies.name: Digital Realty
companies.description: Data center REIT that owns and leases hundreds of data centers worldwide to cloud, AI and enterprise tenants.
companies.explain: One of the two biggest data center landlords in the world. Cloud giants and AI companies rent space and power from it instead of (or alongside) building their own.

companies.name: DigitalBridge

source.quote: With a heritage of more than 30 years investing in and operating businesses across the digital ecosystem, including cell towers, data centers, fiber, small cells, and edge infrastructure, DigitalBridge manages $108 billion of infrastructure assets on behalf of its limited partners and shareholders.

companies.description: Digital infrastructure investment manager (data centers, towers, fiber), owned by SoftBank Group since September 2026.
companies.explain: DigitalBridge's funds took data center operator Switch private in an $11 billion deal; SoftBank bought the firm in 2026 to get a ready-made data center investing platform.

companies.name: Dominion Energy
companies.description: Utility serving Virginia and the Carolinas, including Northern Virginia's 'Data Center Alley'.
companies.explain: Dominion's Virginia utility serves the world's largest cluster of data centers, so its grid buildout is central to how fast AI capacity can grow there.

companies.name: Duke Energy
companies.description: Utility serving the Carolinas, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky.
companies.explain: Duke is one of the largest U.S. utilities and is planning new gas and nuclear capacity as tech companies build data centers in the Carolinas.

companies.name: E&I Engineering
companies.description: Irish maker of switchgear, busway and power distribution for data centers; acquired by Vertiv in 2021.
companies.explain: E&I makes the electrical gear that distributes power inside data centers. Vertiv paid about $1.8 billion for it.

companies.name: Eaton
companies.description: Makes electrical power equipment such as switchgear, UPS systems and power distribution for data centers.
companies.explain: Eaton supplies the electrical equipment that brings power into data centers. It bought Boyd Thermal for $9.5 billion and Fibrebond for $1.4 billion to grow its AI data center business.

companies.name: Energy Capital Partners
companies.description: Private equity firm investing in power generation, renewables and energy infrastructure.
companies.explain: ECP owns and builds power generation, the electricity supply that data centers increasingly compete for.

companies.name: Energy Harbor
companies.description: Former owner of Ohio and Pennsylvania nuclear plants; merged into Vistra in March 2024.
companies.explain: Vistra's purchase of Energy Harbor brought it the Perry, Davis-Besse and Beaver Valley nuclear plants that now supply Meta.

companies.name: Energy Transfer
companies.description: Major U.S. natural gas and oil pipeline partnership.
companies.explain: Energy Transfer supplies natural gas to data centers that make their own power, including Oracle sites and Fermi America's Project Matador.

companies.name: Enfabrica
companies.description: Startup designing networking chips that connect very large numbers of AI processors and memory.
companies.explain: Nvidia reportedly paid over $900M to license Enfabrica's technology and hire its CEO and engineers in 2025.

companies.name: Entergy
companies.description: Utility serving Louisiana, Arkansas, Mississippi and Texas.
companies.explain: Entergy is building gas plants to power Meta's giant Hyperion AI data center in Louisiana and signed a long-term contract to serve Google's data center in West Memphis, Arkansas.

companies.name: Equinix
companies.description: Largest global colocation and interconnection data center company, plus xScale campuses built for hyperscalers.
companies.explain: Equinix runs the data centers where networks and clouds connect. Its xScale joint ventures build large campuses leased to cloud and AI companies.

companies.name: Etched
companies.description: Designs Sohu, an AI chip built only to run transformer models.
companies.explain: Etched is betting that a chip hard-wired for one kind of AI model (transformers) can beat general-purpose GPUs on cost and speed.

companies.name: Fermi America
companies.description: Developer of Project Matador, a planned multi-gigawatt private-power AI campus near Amarillo, Texas.
companies.explain: Fermi plans to generate its own power on site and lease AI data center space. Its first tenant is TensorWave, an AMD-based AI cloud, under a planned $6.5 billion lease.

companies.name: Fervo Energy
companies.description: Developer of enhanced geothermal power plants, including Cape Station in Utah.
companies.explain: Fervo sells round-the-clock geothermal power to Google, including a 396 MW deal for Cape Station in Utah.

companies.name: Fibrebond
companies.description: Builds pre-integrated modular power enclosures for data centers and utilities; acquired by Eaton in 2025.
companies.explain: Fibrebond's factory-built power rooms let data centers get electricity hooked up faster. Eaton bought it for about $1.4 billion.

companies.name: Fidelity Investments
companies.description: Boston-based mutual fund and investment company whose funds buy stakes in private AI companies.
companies.explain: Fidelity's funds co-led Anthropic's $13 billion Series F and joined several xAI rounds.

companies.name: Figure AI

source.quote: Today we’re announcing that we have exceeded more than $1 billion in committed capital through our Series C financing round, at a post-money valuation of $39 billion.

companies.description: Builds general-purpose humanoid robots and the Helix AI system that controls them.
companies.explain: Figure is the best-funded humanoid-robot startup, backed by Nvidia, Intel, Qualcomm and others; its robots need large amounts of AI computing to train.

companies.name: Firmus

source.quote: The transaction brings the company’s total new equity raised over the past year to more than $3bn, and it said its post-money valuation is now above $10.5bn.

companies.description: Australian developer of liquid-cooled AI data centers ('AI factories') running Nvidia GPUs, starting in Tasmania.
companies.explain: Firmus is building Nvidia-based AI data centers across Australia, backed by repeated Nvidia investments and a $10 billion debt facility from Blackstone and Coatue.

companies.name: Fluidstack

source.quote: In January, Fluidstack raised an $830M Series A at a $7.5B valuation, led by Situational Awareness, with participation from world-leading investors.

companies.description: AI cloud and data center developer building custom GPU campuses for frontier labs, including Anthropic.
companies.explain: Fluidstack was picked by Anthropic to build and run custom data centers in Texas and New York as part of a $50 billion US infrastructure plan, turning a small GPU cloud into a major builder.

companies.name: Founders Fund
companies.description: San Francisco venture capital firm co-founded by Peter Thiel.
companies.explain: Founders Fund co-led Anthropic's $30 billion Series G in 2026, part of the venture money pouring into frontier AI labs.

companies.name: Foxconn (Hon Hai)

source.quote: In 2025, revenue totaled TWD8.1 trillion (approx. USD260 billion).

companies.description: World's largest contract electronics maker, building iPhones and AI server racks for Nvidia and cloud companies.
companies.explain: Foxconn assembles a large share of the world's AI server racks, so it collects money from the cloud companies and Nvidia as the AI buildout grows.

companies.name: G42
companies.description: Abu Dhabi-based AI and technology holding company, partly owned by Microsoft.
companies.explain: G42 is the UAE's main AI company and the local partner for huge data center projects such as the UAE Stargate campus; Microsoft owns a minority stake.

companies.name: Galaxy Digital
companies.description: Crypto financial firm that also develops the Helios AI data center campus in West Texas, leased to CoreWeave.
companies.explain: Galaxy turned its Helios bitcoin mining site into an AI data center campus. CoreWeave has leased all 800 MW of approved power there under 15-year leases.

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.description: Makes gas turbines, grid equipment and wind turbines for power generation.
companies.explain: GE Vernova builds the gas turbines that many AI data centers are ordering to make their own electricity, such as Crusoe's 29-turbine order.

companies.name: GIC
companies.description: Singapore's sovereign wealth fund, managing the country's foreign reserves.
companies.explain: GIC co-led Anthropic's $30 billion Series G in February 2026 and co-led the $65 billion Series H, putting Singapore's reserves behind one of the largest AI labs.

companies.name: GlobalFoundries
companies.description: Contract chipmaker focused on mature and specialty processes, with fabs in New York, Vermont, Germany and Singapore.
companies.explain: GlobalFoundries makes the less cutting-edge but essential chips (radio, power, networking) that sit around AI processors. It began as AMD's spun-off factories and counts AMD, Qualcomm and Apple as customers.

companies.name: Alphabet (Google)

source.quote: As of June 30, 2026, we had $519.5 billion of remaining performance obligations (“revenue backlog”), of which $513.9 billion related to Google Cloud.

companies.description: Parent of Google; builds Gemini AI models and rents its own TPU AI chips and other computing power through Google Cloud.
companies.explain: Google Cloud sells computing power, especially its in-house TPU chips, to AI labs such as Anthropic and Meta. Its contracted backlog jumped past $500 billion in 2026 as those labs signed huge multi-year deals. The backlog figure here is the Google Cloud portion.

companies.name: Great Lakes Data Racks & Cabinets
companies.description: Maker of data center racks and cabinets; acquired by Vertiv in 2025.
companies.explain: Great Lakes builds the racks that hold servers, including dense AI hardware. Vertiv paid $200 million for it.

companies.name: Greenoaks
companies.description: San Francisco growth investment firm backing AI labs such as Safe Superintelligence and Anthropic.
companies.explain: Greenoaks led Safe Superintelligence's 2025 round and co-led Anthropic's $65 billion Series H.

companies.name: Groq
companies.description: Designs LPU chips for fast AI inference and runs the GroqCloud inference service.
companies.explain: Groq built a chip designed to run AI models quickly. In December 2025 Nvidia paid about $17B to license its technology and hire its founder and many engineers, while Groq kept running its cloud.

companies.name: Habana Labs
companies.description: Israeli designer of Gaudi AI training and inference chips; part of Intel since 2019.
companies.explain: Intel bought Habana for about $2B in 2019; its Gaudi chips became Intel's main AI accelerator line.

companies.name: Helion Energy
companies.description: Fusion energy startup building its first commercial fusion power plant in Washington state.
companies.explain: Helion signed the world's first fusion power purchase agreement, with Microsoft, for power from 2028; OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is a major backer.

companies.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise
companies.description: Makes servers, storage and networking equipment, including AI systems and Juniper networking.
companies.explain: HPE sells AI servers and, since buying Juniper for about $14 billion in 2025, a large networking business for data centers.

companies.name: Humain
companies.description: Saudi Arabia's national AI company, owned by the Public Investment Fund, building data centers and AI models.
companies.explain: Humain is Saudi Arabia's vehicle for buying large amounts of AI chips and building data centers, with deals across Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm and US clouds.

companies.name: Hut 8
companies.description: Energy and digital infrastructure company developing AI data center campuses in Louisiana and Texas.
companies.explain: Hut 8 leases its River Bend campus to Fluidstack under a $7 billion, 15-year lease backstopped by Google, and its Beacon Point campus to an unnamed investment-grade tenant.

companies.name: ICONIQ
companies.description: San Francisco investment firm and family office for tech founders, with a growth-stage venture arm.
companies.explain: ICONIQ led Anthropic's $13 billion Series F in September 2025 and co-led later rounds, making it one of the lab's biggest financial backers.

companies.name: Infinera
companies.description: Maker of optical networking equipment and optical chips; acquired by Nokia in February 2025.
companies.explain: Infinera's optical gear connects data centers over long distances. Nokia bought it for $2.3 billion to sell more to cloud companies.

companies.name: Inflection AI
companies.description: AI company that built the Pi chatbot, now focused on enterprise AI after most staff joined Microsoft in 2024.
companies.explain: Inflection is an example of a 'license and hire' deal: Microsoft paid about $650 million and hired most of its team instead of buying the company.

companies.name: Innovium
companies.description: Designer of Ethernet switch chips for cloud data centers; part of Marvell since 2021.
companies.explain: Marvell bought Innovium for $1.1B in stock to add data-center switch chips.

companies.name: Inphi
companies.description: Designer of high-speed optical and electrical data-connection chips; part of Marvell since 2021.
companies.explain: Marvell bought Inphi for about $10B; its optical chips now carry much of the data flowing between AI servers.

companies.name: Intel
companies.description: US chipmaker that designs PC and server processors and is building a contract manufacturing (foundry) business.
companies.explain: Intel is the main US-owned maker of leading-edge chips. Struggling to keep up, it has raised money from Nvidia, SoftBank, the US government and private-equity partners while trying to win foundry customers like Microsoft and Amazon.

companies.name: Intersect

source.quote: Kirkland & Ellis advised a group of investors in Intersect on a definitive agreement to sell Intersect, which provides data center and energy infrastructure solutions, for $4.75 billion in cash, plus the assumption of debt, to Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG).

companies.description: Developer of power plants and co-located data center campuses; being acquired by Alphabet.
companies.explain: Alphabet agreed to buy Intersect for $4.75B plus debt so Google can build data centers together with their own new power supply.

companies.name: IREN

source.quote: As of June 30, 2026, the Group’s unsatisfied remaining performance obligations under ASC 606 and the aggregate contracted value of lease arrangements under ASC 842 totaled approximately $16.6 billion.

companies.description: Former bitcoin miner (Iris Energy) turned AI cloud, renting Nvidia GPUs from its own powered data centers in Texas and Canada.
companies.explain: IREN converted cheap power and bitcoin-mining sites into AI data centers and signed big GPU rental deals with Microsoft and Nvidia. Nvidia is both its chip supplier and a customer, and holds rights to invest up to $2.1 billion.

companies.name: Juniper Networks
companies.description: Maker of network routers, switches and security gear; acquired by HPE in July 2025.
companies.explain: Juniper's routers and data center switches are now part of HPE, which paid about $14 billion for it.

companies.name: Kairos Power
companies.description: Private developer of molten-salt-cooled small nuclear reactors, building demonstration units in Oak Ridge, Tennessee.
companies.explain: Kairos signed the first corporate deal for a fleet of small reactors (500 MW for Google) and a power deal with TVA for its Hermes 2 plant.

companies.name: Kioxia

source.quote: Revenue increased 37% YoY to ¥2.34 trillion, while operating profit nearly doubled to ¥870 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders rose to ¥554 billion.

companies.description: Japanese NAND flash memory maker, formerly Toshiba Memory, which runs joint factories with Sandisk.
companies.explain: Kioxia makes the flash memory chips inside data center SSDs. Its factories in Japan are shared with Sandisk, which pays Kioxia for supply. Revenue converted from about ¥2.34 trillion at roughly ¥150 per dollar.

companies.name: KKR

source.quote: Assets Under Management (“AUM”) of $796 billion, up 16% year-over-year

companies.description: Global private equity and infrastructure investor that owns data center operators such as CyrusOne.
companies.explain: KKR buys and grows data center landlords with its infrastructure funds; it took CyrusOne private with GIP in a roughly $15 billion deal.

companies.name: KLA
companies.description: US maker of inspection and measurement equipment that finds defects during chip manufacturing.
companies.explain: As AI chips get more complex, chipmakers spend more on KLA's tools to catch defects and keep yields up.

companies.name: Kokusai Electric
companies.description: Japanese maker of batch wafer processing equipment (deposition and treatment) used in memory and logic chip factories.
companies.explain: Kokusai Electric makes tools that coat many wafers at once, important for 3D memory chips. Applied Materials tried to buy it from KKR in 2019-2021 but the deal failed.

companies.name: Lam Research
companies.description: US maker of chipmaking equipment, especially etch and deposition tools used heavily in memory and advanced logic.
companies.explain: Lam's tools are needed to build the stacked memory (HBM, NAND) and advanced chips used in AI servers, so fab spending by Samsung, SK hynix, TSMC and Micron flows to it.

companies.name: Lambda
companies.description: AI cloud that rents Nvidia GPU clusters to developers and big tech, and builds its own AI data centers.
companies.explain: Lambda rents Nvidia GPUs to customers including Microsoft, and was reported to rent GPU servers back to Nvidia itself. Nvidia is also an investor, a common loop among neoclouds.

companies.name: Lancium
companies.description: Texas energy and data center campus developer; owns the Abilene site behind the first Stargate campus.
companies.explain: Lancium secures land and grid power in West Texas and develops campuses on it, including the Abilene site built out with Crusoe for Oracle and OpenAI.

companies.name: Lightmatter
companies.description: Designs photonic chips and interconnects that use light to move data between AI processors.
companies.explain: Lightmatter is a startup using light instead of electricity to connect AI chips, aiming to make very large AI clusters faster and less power hungry.

companies.name: Lightspeed Venture Partners
companies.description: Venture capital firm based in Menlo Park, California, and a major investor in Anthropic.
companies.explain: Lightspeed led Anthropic's $3.5 billion Series E in 2025 and co-led its $13 billion Series F, helping fund Anthropic's huge cloud computing bills.

companies.name: LS Power
companies.description: Private power and transmission developer and investor.
companies.explain: LS Power sold NRG 13 GW of gas plants and the CPower demand-response business for about $12B, closed January 2026.

companies.name: Lumentum
companies.description: Makes lasers and optical components and modules for data center and telecom networks.
companies.explain: Lumentum makes the lasers inside the optical links between AI chips. Nvidia agreed in 2026 to invest $2 billion in it and to buy billions of dollars of its lasers.

companies.name: Marvell Technology
companies.description: Designs custom AI chips, optical and networking chips that move data inside and between data centers.
companies.explain: Marvell makes custom chips for cloud giants such as Amazon and the optical links that tie AI servers together, and has bought several connectivity startups to grow that business.

companies.name: MediaTek
companies.description: Taiwanese chip designer of smartphone, TV and networking processors, expanding into custom data-center AI chips.
companies.explain: MediaTek is one of the world's largest fabless chip designers (it designs chips and has others manufacture them) and is pushing into custom AI chips for data centers.

companies.name: Mellanox Technologies
companies.description: Israeli designer of high-speed InfiniBand and Ethernet networking chips; part of Nvidia since 2020.
companies.explain: Nvidia bought Mellanox for $6.9B, and its networking technology became the backbone that links GPUs together in Nvidia's AI systems.

companies.name: Menlo Ventures
companies.description: Venture capital firm based in the San Francisco Bay Area and an early Anthropic investor.
companies.explain: Menlo Ventures is a long-time Anthropic investor and took part in its $3.5 billion Series E in 2025.

companies.name: Meta Platforms
companies.description: Owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp; builds the Llama AI models and some of the largest AI data centers.
companies.explain: Meta is one of the biggest spenders on AI data centers and chips, paid for out of its advertising profits, and bought a 49% stake in Scale AI.

companies.name: MGX
companies.description: Abu Dhabi state-backed technology investment firm focused on AI and semiconductors, founded by Mubadala and G42.
companies.explain: MGX puts Gulf state money into AI: it is an equity funder of Stargate, a partner in the BlackRock-led AI Infrastructure Partnership that bought Aligned Data Centers, and an investor in OpenAI, xAI and Anthropic.

companies.name: Micron Technology
companies.description: US maker of DRAM, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and NAND flash, the only large US-based memory chipmaker.
companies.explain: Every AI chip needs memory next to it. Micron is one of only three companies that make high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for Nvidia and AMD accelerators, so AI spending flows straight into its sales.

companies.name: Microsoft

source.quote: Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations related to the commercial portion of revenue was $678 billion as of June 30, 2026, with a weighted average duration of approximately 2.3 years.

companies.description: Software and cloud giant that runs the Azure cloud and is OpenAI's largest outside investor and main cloud partner.
companies.explain: Microsoft rents huge amounts of computing power through Azure. AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic have promised to spend hundreds of billions of dollars on Azure, which shows up as Microsoft's contracted backlog.

companies.name: Mistral AI

source.quote: Sacra estimated annualized revenue at $400M in January 2026.

companies.description: Paris-based maker of open and commercial AI models and the Le Chat assistant.
companies.explain: Mistral is Europe's leading AI lab; its backers include chip-equipment maker ASML, Nvidia and Samsung, and it is building its own data centers in France.

companies.name: Motivair
companies.description: Buffalo, New York maker of liquid cooling systems for supercomputers and AI; majority-owned by Schneider Electric since 2025.
companies.explain: Motivair makes liquid cooling for AI servers. Schneider Electric paid $850 million for 75% of it.

companies.name: Nebius

source.quote: As of June 30, 2026, the amount of unsatisfied RPO was $37,490.6, of which 36% is expected to be recognized as revenue during the 24 months ending June 30, 2028, 40% between months 25 and 48, and the remainder recognized thereafter.

companies.description: Amsterdam-based AI cloud (spun out of Yandex) that rents Nvidia GPU capacity to Microsoft, Meta and AI developers.
companies.explain: Nebius turned large multi-year contracts from Microsoft and Meta into a fast-growing AI cloud, and Nvidia invested $2 billion in it. Its backlog of contracted revenue is many times its current annual sales.

companies.name: NeoPhotonics
companies.description: Maker of lasers and optical components for data center and telecom links; acquired by Lumentum in 2022.
companies.explain: NeoPhotonics made high-speed lasers for optical networks. Lumentum paid about $918 million for it.

companies.name: NextEra Energy
companies.description: Owner of Florida Power & Light and NextEra Energy Resources, the largest U.S. wind and solar developer.
companies.explain: NextEra builds and sells clean power to tech companies: it is restarting Iowa's Duane Arnold nuclear plant for Google and signed about 2.5 GW of solar and storage contracts with Meta.

companies.name: Nokia

source.quote: From the consolidated income statement Net sales 19 889 19 220 21 138

companies.description: Makes mobile, optical, IP and data center networking equipment and licenses telecom patents.
companies.explain: Nokia sells network equipment to telecoms and cloud companies, including data center switches to Microsoft. Nvidia bought a $1 billion stake in 2025, and Nokia bought Infinera to sell more optical gear to hyperscalers.

companies.name: Northern Data
companies.description: German AI cloud and data center operator (Taiga Cloud, Ardent); majority-owned by Rumble since June 2026.
companies.explain: Northern Data runs one of Europe's larger Nvidia GPU fleets. Long controlled by stablecoin issuer Tether, it was taken over by video platform Rumble in an all-stock deal completed in June 2026.

companies.name: NRG Energy
companies.description: Power generator and retail electricity provider in Texas and the Northeast.
companies.explain: NRG doubled its power plant fleet to about 25 GW by buying LS Power's gas plants, betting on rising electricity demand from data centers.

companies.name: Nscale

source.quote: This round values Nscale at $14.6 billion.

companies.description: London-based AI cloud building GPU campuses in the UK, Norway, Portugal and Texas, with Microsoft as anchor customer.
companies.explain: Nscale grew from a small European cloud into a major Microsoft supplier in about two years, funded by investors including Nvidia, Dell and Nokia, the companies that sell it hardware.

companies.name: Nubis Communications
companies.description: Startup making compact, low-power optical and electrical interconnects for AI; acquired by Ciena in 2025.
companies.explain: Nubis builds links that move data between AI chips. Ciena paid $270 million for it.

companies.name: NuScale Power
companies.description: Developer of the NuScale small modular reactor, the first SMR design certified by the U.S. NRC.
companies.explain: NuScale's approved small-reactor design is a candidate to power data centers, though it has no large AI customer contract yet.

companies.name: Nuvia
companies.description: CPU design startup founded by former Apple chip architects; part of Qualcomm since 2021.
companies.explain: Qualcomm bought Nuvia to design its own high-performance processors, now used in its PC chips and planned data-center CPUs.

companies.name: Nvidia
companies.description: Designs the GPUs, networking and full AI server systems that most AI models are trained and run on.
companies.explain: Nvidia sells the chips nearly every AI lab and cloud depends on, so a large share of AI spending ends up as Nvidia revenue. It also reinvests that cash into its own customers, such as OpenAI and neoclouds.

companies.name: Oklo
companies.description: Developer of Aurora small fast-neutron nuclear reactors ('powerhouses') that sell power to customers.
companies.explain: Oklo has no operating reactors yet but has signed large AI-related power agreements, including a 12 GW framework with Switch and a Meta prepayment for a 1.2 GW campus in Ohio.

companies.name: OpenAI

source.quote: the company's annualized revenue has surpassed $20 billion in 2025, up from $6 billion in 2024 with growth closely tracking an expansion in computing capacity.
OpenAI has closed its latest financing round with $122bn in committed capital, giving the AI company a post-money valuation of $852bn.

companies.description: Maker of ChatGPT and the GPT models; restructured in 2025 into OpenAI Group PBC controlled by the OpenAI Foundation.
companies.explain: OpenAI is the biggest buyer in the AI money web: it has promised hundreds of billions of dollars to cloud and chip companies, and raises record sums from Microsoft, Amazon, Nvidia and SoftBank to pay for it.

companies.name: Oracle

source.quote: Remaining performance obligations were $664 billion and $455 billion as of August 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

companies.description: Database and business-software company whose Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) builds giant AI data centers for OpenAI and others.
companies.explain: Oracle turned into a major AI landlord: OpenAI's reported $300 billion contract and deals with Meta and Nvidia pushed its contracted backlog to $664 billion, much of it from a few AI customers.

companies.name: Pensando Systems
companies.description: Designer of data processing unit (DPU) networking chips; part of AMD since 2022.
companies.explain: AMD bought Pensando for $1.9B; its networking chips are part of AMD's AI server racks.

companies.name: Perplexity

source.quote: Perplexity's ‌annualised revenue ⁠has risen to more than $US750 million ($A1 billion) from less ​than $US250 million ($A349 million) at the start of the year, the report said.
Perplexity has reportedly raised $200 million in fresh funding, pushing its valuation to $20 billion barely two months after it secured $100 million at an $18 billion valuation.

companies.description: AI-powered answer engine and Comet browser that searches the web and cites sources.
companies.explain: Perplexity rents its computing from clouds such as Microsoft Azure and competes with Google search; investors include Nvidia.

companies.name: Everpure (formerly Pure Storage)
companies.description: US maker of all-flash data storage systems; renamed from Pure Storage to Everpure in January 2026.
companies.explain: Pure sells flash-based storage that replaces hard disks. It won a deal for Meta to use its flash technology in Meta's next-generation data centers, a sign hyperscalers are moving AI data onto flash.

companies.name: PurgeRite
companies.description: Provides flushing, purging and filtration services for data center liquid cooling systems; acquired by Vertiv in 2025.
companies.explain: PurgeRite prepares and maintains the pipes of liquid cooling systems. Vertiv paid about $1 billion for it.

companies.name: Qatar Investment Authority
companies.description: Qatar's sovereign wealth fund, investing the state's oil and gas income worldwide.
companies.explain: QIA is part of a wave of Gulf state money flowing into AI labs, joining xAI's Series C and Series E rounds.

companies.name: QTS Data Centers

source.quote: will acquire all outstanding shares of common stock of QTS Realty Trust for $78.00 per share in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $10 billion

companies.description: Hyperscale data center developer and operator owned by Blackstone since 2021.
companies.explain: QTS builds giant data center campuses leased to cloud and AI companies. Blackstone bought it for about $10 billion (including debt) in 2021 and has poured billions more into expansion.

companies.name: Qualcomm
companies.description: Designs smartphone processors and modems, and since 2025 data-center AI inference chips (AI200/AI250).
companies.explain: Best known for phone chips, Qualcomm is moving into AI data centers, with Saudi Arabia's Humain as its first big customer and acquisitions like Alphawave to build out the business.

companies.name: Rapidus
companies.description: Japanese startup chipmaker building a 2nm factory in Hokkaido, backed by the Japanese government and major Japanese companies.
companies.explain: Rapidus is Japan's bid to make leading-edge chips at home again, using technology licensed from IBM. It is funded mostly by government subsidies plus investment from companies like Toyota, Sony, NTT and Kioxia.

companies.name: Reflection AI

source.quote: This investment has propelled the company’s valuation to a striking $8 billion.

companies.description: AI lab founded by former DeepMind researchers, building open-weight frontier models.
companies.explain: Reflection AI is backed heavily by Nvidia, which led its $2 billion round; that money mostly buys computing to train its models.

companies.name: Rivos
companies.description: Startup designing RISC-V CPUs and AI accelerators; agreed to be acquired by Meta in 2025.
companies.explain: Meta agreed to buy Rivos to speed up its in-house AI chip program and reduce its reliance on Nvidia.

companies.name: Safe Superintelligence (SSI)
companies.description: AI lab co-founded by former OpenAI chief scientist Ilya Sutskever, focused only on building safe superintelligence.
companies.explain: SSI has no products yet but raised billions from investors including Alphabet and Nvidia, and rents Google's TPU chips for its research.

companies.name: SambaNova
companies.description: Designs reconfigurable dataflow (RDU) AI chips and sells AI systems and cloud inference.
companies.explain: SambaNova is a venture-backed AI chip startup. Intel discussed buying it in 2025 and instead became an investor and partner in 2026.

companies.name: Samsung Electronics
companies.description: Korean electronics giant that makes memory chips (DRAM, HBM, flash) and runs the world's second-largest contract chip foundry.
companies.explain: Samsung both sells memory used in AI servers and manufactures chips for other companies, such as Tesla's next AI chips at its Texas fab. It competes with TSMC and SK hynix.

companies.name: Sandisk
companies.description: US maker of NAND flash memory and SSDs, spun off from Western Digital in February 2025.
companies.explain: AI data centers store huge amounts of data on flash drives. Sandisk co-owns flash factories in Japan with Kioxia and sells the SSDs that AI servers use.

companies.name: Scale AI

source.quote: Scale AI, co-founded by CEO Alexandr Wang in 2016, reported $870m in revenue last year and anticipates sales to exceed $2bn in 2025.
KUALA LUMPUR: Meta Platforms has finalised an investment in Scale AI that values the startup at over US$29 billion, Scale AI said on Thursday.

companies.description: Provides labeled training data and AI evaluation services to AI labs, companies and governments.
companies.explain: Scale AI supplies the human-labeled data that labs use to train models; Meta owns 49% of it after a $14.3 billion investment in 2025.

companies.name: Schneider Electric

source.quote: Full-year revenue rose 8.9% organically to €40.2 billion, crossing €40 billion for the first time, while fourth-quarter sales increased 10.7% organically to a record €11.1 billion.

companies.description: Makes electrical power, cooling and automation equipment, including data center power and cooling systems.
companies.explain: Schneider Electric is one of the biggest suppliers of power and cooling gear to data centers. Builders like Switch, Digital Realty and Compass have reserved billions of dollars of its factory output.

companies.name: Seagate Technology
companies.description: Hard disk drive maker (Irish-incorporated, executive offices in Singapore) supplying mass storage to cloud data centers.
companies.explain: Seagate and Western Digital make nearly all the world's hard drives. Cloud giants buy them in bulk to store the data AI models are trained on.

companies.name: Sequoia Capital
companies.description: Venture capital firm based in Menlo Park, California, investing in AI labs and AI software companies.
companies.explain: Sequoia is a repeat backer of frontier AI labs: it co-led Anthropic's $65 billion Series H and invested in xAI and Safe Superintelligence.

companies.name: SK hynix

source.quote: announced today that it has achieved record financial results in 2025 – 97.1467 trillion won in revenue, 47.2063 trillion won in operating profit (with an operating margin of 49%), and 42.9479 trillion won in net profit (with a net margin of 44%).

companies.description: South Korean memory maker and the largest supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI chips.
companies.explain: SK hynix makes most of the HBM memory that sits next to Nvidia's AI chips, which made it one of the biggest winners of the AI build-out. Revenue converted from 97.15 trillion won at roughly 1,420 won per dollar (2025 average).

companies.name: SoftBank Group
companies.description: Japanese tech holding company and Vision Fund investor; OpenAI's largest outside backer and owner of Arm and Ampere.
companies.explain: SoftBank has put about $65 billion into OpenAI, leads the Stargate data center project, and bought chip designer Ampere and data center investor DigitalBridge, making it one of the biggest sources of cash in the AI build-out.

companies.name: Southern Company
companies.description: Utility holding company that owns Georgia Power, Alabama Power and Mississippi Power.
companies.explain: Southern's Georgia Power is adding large amounts of generation to serve a wave of data center projects in the Atlanta area.

companies.name: SpaceX
companies.description: Rocket, Starlink and AI company; owns xAI (Grok, X) since February 2026 and Cursor maker Anysphere since August 2026.
companies.explain: SpaceX became an AI lab by buying xAI and Cursor, so the AI spending of both now sits inside a public company that also earns cash from Starlink and launches.

companies.name: STACK Infrastructure
companies.description: Private developer and operator of hyperscale and wholesale data center campuses worldwide.
companies.explain: STACK builds and leases big data center campuses to cloud providers, part of the landlord layer that AI compute depends on.

companies.name: Stargate (OpenAI/SoftBank/Oracle/MGX venture)
companies.description: Joint venture announced Jan 2025 to build AI data centers for OpenAI in the US; equity from SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle and MGX.
companies.explain: Stargate is the vehicle OpenAI and its partners use to fund AI data centers, with a stated plan of $500 billion over four years. SoftBank has financial responsibility and OpenAI operational responsibility. hq_state reflects a US entity; no HQ city has been announced.

companies.name: Supermicro
companies.description: Designs and builds servers and rack-scale systems, including GPU servers for AI.
companies.explain: Supermicro assembles Nvidia GPU servers for AI labs and cloud companies, so much of the money spent on AI hardware passes through it.

companies.name: Switch

source.quote: for $34.25 per share in cash, or approximately $11 billion, including the repayment of outstanding debt.

companies.description: Operator of large data center campuses in Nevada, Arizona, Georgia and Michigan, owned by DigitalBridge and IFM.
companies.explain: Switch runs huge campuses such as its Las Vegas and Reno sites that are increasingly leased for AI. DigitalBridge and IFM took it private for about $11 billion including debt in 2022.

companies.name: Talen Energy
companies.description: Independent power producer that owns the Susquehanna nuclear plant in Pennsylvania and gas plants.
companies.explain: Talen sold Amazon a data center campus next to its Susquehanna nuclear plant and agreed to supply Amazon up to 1,920 MW of nuclear power through 2042, one of the first big nuclear-for-AI deals.

companies.name: TensorWave

source.quote: Its valuation of $1.55 billion is more than four times the roughly $400 million valuation reportedly linked to TensorWave’s $100 million Series A in May 2025.

companies.description: Las Vegas-based AI cloud built entirely on AMD Instinct GPUs.
companies.explain: TensorWave is AMD's showcase cloud: it runs only AMD GPUs and AMD's venture arm co-led its funding rounds, so AMD money helps buy AMD chips.

companies.name: Tenstorrent
companies.description: Designs RISC-V CPUs and AI accelerator chips and licenses its chip designs.
companies.explain: Tenstorrent, led by veteran chip architect Jim Keller, sells AI chips and licenses its designs, positioning itself as an open alternative to Nvidia.

companies.name: TeraWulf
companies.description: Bitcoin miner turned AI data center developer with campuses in New York, Texas and Kentucky.
companies.explain: TeraWulf leases AI data center space to Fluidstack (with Google backing the rent), G42's Core42 and, from 2026, Anthropic directly.

companies.name: TerraPower
companies.description: Bill Gates-founded developer of the Natrium sodium-cooled reactor, building its first plant in Kemmerer, Wyoming.
companies.explain: Meta is funding TerraPower Natrium reactors for its data centers, and Nvidia invested in TerraPower's $650M 2025 fundraise.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.description: Electric car, battery and robotics company that trains its own self-driving AI and invested in xAI.
companies.explain: Tesla buys large amounts of AI computing for self-driving and robots, sells Megapack batteries to AI data centers, and holds a stake in xAI (now SpaceX shares).

companies.name: Thinking Machines Lab

source.quote: The deal, which includes participation from Nvidia, Accel, ServiceNow, CISCO, AMD, and Jane Street, values the startup at $12 billion, the spokesperson said.

companies.description: AI lab founded in 2025 by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati; releases the Inkling open-weight models.
companies.explain: Thinking Machines raised a record $2 billion seed round from investors including Nvidia, AMD and Cisco, money that mostly goes to renting AI chips.

companies.name: Thrive Capital
companies.description: New York venture capital firm founded by Josh Kushner and a large early backer of OpenAI.
companies.explain: Thrive led OpenAI's $6.6 billion funding round in October 2024, one of the largest venture rounds at the time.

companies.name: Together AI

source.quote: Together AI, a San Francisco-based company specialising in open-source AI models, has raised $800m in a Series C financing round, bringing its post-money valuation to $8.3bn.

companies.description: AI cloud focused on running and training open-source models, selling both API access and GPU clusters.
companies.explain: Together AI sells AI model access and GPU clusters to developers, and itself rents capacity from other neoclouds such as IREN. Nvidia has invested in its rounds.

companies.name: Tokyo Electron
companies.description: Japan's largest chipmaking equipment maker, known for coater/developer, etch and deposition tools.
companies.explain: Tokyo Electron supplies tools to every major chip factory; it benefits when TSMC, Samsung, Intel and memory makers expand capacity for AI chips.

companies.name: Tower Semiconductor
companies.description: Israeli contract chipmaker specializing in analog, radio-frequency and silicon photonics chips.
companies.explain: Tower makes specialty chips, including optical (silicon photonics) parts used in AI data center networking. Intel tried to buy it for $5.4 billion in 2022 before the deal collapsed.

companies.name: TSMC

source.quote: As a leader of the foundry segment, our net revenue and net income attributable to shareholders of the parent were NT$2,894,308 million and NT$1,158,380 million in 2024, and NT$3,809,054 million (US$121,423 million) and NT$1,697,604 million (US$54,116 million) in 2025, respectively.

companies.description: The world's largest contract chipmaker; manufactures most advanced AI chips for Nvidia, AMD, Apple, Broadcom and others.
companies.explain: Almost every leading AI chip, from Nvidia GPUs to Google TPUs, is made in TSMC's factories, so AI spending flows through it. Revenue shown is TSMC's own US dollar translation of its NT$3.81 trillion 2025 revenue.

companies.name: Tennessee Valley Authority
companies.description: U.S. federally owned power company serving Tennessee and parts of six nearby states.
companies.explain: TVA is the government-owned utility for the Tennessee Valley; it signed the first U.S. utility deal to buy power from Kairos Power's advanced reactor, supplying Google's data centers.

companies.name: U.S. Government
companies.description: The U.S. federal government, which funds chip factories and energy projects through CHIPS Act grants, loans and equity stakes.
companies.explain: Washington pays tens of billions to bring chipmaking and power to the US: CHIPS Act grants to Intel, TSMC, Samsung and Micron, a roughly 10% equity stake in Intel, and Energy Department loans for nuclear power and power lines.

companies.name: Valor Equity Partners
companies.description: Chicago private equity firm led by Antonio Gracias, a long-time investor in Elon Musk's companies.
companies.explain: Valor invested in xAI's Series B, C and E rounds, which together raised $32 billion to pay for xAI's supercomputers.

companies.name: Vantage Data Centers
companies.description: Private hyperscale data center developer building campuses in North America, EMEA and Asia-Pacific.
companies.explain: Vantage builds very large campuses for cloud and AI tenants, including the Lighthouse campus in Wisconsin for Oracle and OpenAI's Stargate and the 1.4 GW Frontier campus in Texas.

companies.name: VAST Data

source.quote: High Growth, Built for Durability The Company has surpassed $4 billion in cumulative bookings and exited the previous fiscal year with more than $500 million in Committed Annual Recurring Revenue (CARR), along with positive operating margin and free cash flow.

VAST Data, the AI Operating System company, today announced the closing of its Series F financing at a $30 billion valuation, representing more than a threefold increase from its $9.1 billion Series E valuation in late 2023.

companies.description: Private maker of data storage and database software for AI clusters, used by CoreWeave and other GPU clouds.
companies.explain: AI training needs huge amounts of data delivered fast to GPUs. VAST sells the software layer that stores and serves that data, and GPU clouds like CoreWeave have signed billion-dollar deals for it. Revenue shown is committed annual recurring revenue, not audited revenue.

companies.name: Vertiv
companies.description: Makes power and cooling equipment for data centers, including liquid cooling for AI servers.
companies.explain: Vertiv supplies the power systems and cooling (including liquid cooling) that keep AI data centers running. It has been buying smaller cooling and rack makers to keep up with AI demand.

companies.name: Vistra
companies.description: Texas-based power producer and retailer with one of the largest U.S. nuclear and gas fleets.
companies.explain: Vistra sells power from big nuclear and gas plants; it signed 20-year deals to supply Meta with 2.6 GW from its Ohio and Pennsylvania nuclear plants and keeps buying gas plants to meet data center demand.

companies.name: Voltage Park
companies.description: Nonprofit-backed AI cloud renting Nvidia H100 GPU capacity at low cost to AI researchers and startups.
companies.explain: Voltage Park was funded by a philanthropic foundation to buy tens of thousands of Nvidia GPUs and rent them cheaply, adding supply outside the big clouds.

companies.name: Vultr

source.quote: The transaction, which was announced on December 18, values Vultr at $3.5 billion.

companies.description: Cloud computing provider that added AMD and Nvidia GPU clusters for AI workloads.
companies.explain: Vultr is one of the few clouds betting heavily on AMD GPUs, and AMD's venture arm co-led its first big funding round.

companies.name: WEKA

source.quote: The company exceeded over $100 million in annual recurring revenue and grew to more than 500 employees globally, as five of its customers expanded their AI and HPC clusters to over an EB of data under management running on the Weka Data Platform.

WEKA, the AI-native data platform company, has raised $140 million in an oversubscribed Series E funding round comprised of a combined primary and secondary transaction led by Valor Equity Partners, a previous investor in the company.

companies.description: Private maker of high-speed data storage software that keeps GPUs supplied with data in AI clusters.
companies.explain: WEKA competes with VAST Data to sell the storage software GPU clouds use for AI training. Nvidia, Micron, Samsung and HPE are among its investors.

companies.name: Western Digital
companies.description: US maker of high-capacity hard disk drives used in cloud and AI data centers.
companies.explain: Most of the world's data still sits on hard drives. Western Digital sells the big drives cloud companies use to store AI training data, and says its capacity is booked out by large customers.

companies.name: Westinghouse Electric Company
companies.description: Nuclear reactor designer (AP1000) and fuel supplier, owned by Brookfield and Cameco.
companies.explain: Westinghouse's AP1000 is the main large U.S. reactor design; AI power demand and government support have revived plans for new AP1000 plants.

companies.name: Williams Companies
companies.description: Natural gas pipeline company (Transco) that also builds dedicated on-site power plants for data centers.
companies.explain: Williams' 'Power Innovation' business builds gas power plants next to data centers, starting with the Socrates project serving Meta in Ohio.

companies.name: X-energy
companies.description: Developer of the Xe-100 high-temperature gas-cooled small modular reactor and TRISO-X nuclear fuel.
companies.explain: Amazon is an investor and anchor customer, with options for more than 5 GW of X-energy reactors by 2039 to power its data centers.

companies.name: xAI

source.quote: The transaction values SpaceX at US$1 trillion, and xAI at US$250 billion, according to a person familiar with the matter.

companies.description: Elon Musk's AI company, maker of the Grok models and owner of X; a wholly owned subsidiary of SpaceX since February 2026.
companies.explain: xAI builds some of the largest GPU supercomputers (Colossus) and buys huge volumes of Nvidia chips; since SpaceX bought it, its spending is funded by SpaceX.

companies.name: Xcel Energy
companies.description: Utility serving Minnesota, Colorado, Texas, New Mexico and other states.
companies.explain: Xcel will power Google's new Minnesota data center, with Google paying for 1.9 GW of new wind, solar and storage on Xcel's grid.

companies.name: Xilinx
companies.description: Designer of programmable (FPGA) and adaptive chips; part of AMD since February 2022.
companies.explain: AMD's $35B all-stock purchase of Xilinx was one of the biggest chip deals ever and strengthened AMD's data-center business.

companies.name: ZT Systems
companies.description: Designs and builds rack-scale AI and cloud servers for hyperscalers; acquired by AMD in 2025.
companies.explain: ZT Systems built custom server racks for the largest cloud companies. AMD bought it for $4.9 billion to sell complete AI systems, then sold the factory part to Sanmina.

deals.title: AMD amends wafer supply agreement with GlobalFoundries

sources.quote: On January 28, 2019, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (the “Company”) entered into a seventh amendment (the “Seventh Amendment”) to the Wafer Supply Agreement with GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. (“GF”).

deals.explain: AMD, which spun off its factories as GlobalFoundries in 2009, agreed to new yearly wafer purchase targets and pricing with GF for 2019-2021 while gaining freedom to make its newest 7nm chips elsewhere (at TSMC). AMD pays GF for wafers, and pays a penalty if it misses the targets. Dollar amounts were not disclosed.

deals.title: Nvidia buys Mellanox for $6.9B

sources.quote: Pursuant to the agreement, NVIDIA will acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Mellanox for $125 per share in cash, representing a total enterprise value of approximately $6.9 billion.

deals.explain: Nvidia bought Israeli networking-chip maker Mellanox for about $6.9B in cash, closing in April 2020. Mellanox's high-speed links became the networking backbone of Nvidia's AI data-center systems.

deals.title: Applied Materials agrees to buy Kokusai Electric for $2.2B

sources.quote: Subject to the terms and conditions set forth in the Share Purchase Agreement, at the Closing, Buyer will pay $2.2 billion in cash for the Company, subject to adjustments for net debt, transaction expenses and net working capital, as further described in the Share Purchase Agreement.
(Nasdaq: AMAT) today announced a definitive agreement under which Applied will acquire all outstanding shares of Kokusai Electric Corporation

deals.explain: Applied Materials, the largest US chip-equipment maker, agreed to buy Japanese equipment maker Kokusai Electric from private-equity firm KKR for $2.2 billion in cash. The price was later raised to $3.5 billion, and the deal ultimately collapsed.

deals.title: Cisco agrees to buy optical-module maker Acacia for $2.6B

sources.quote: Under the terms of the agreement, Cisco has agreed to acquire Acacia for $70.00 per share in cash, or for approximately $2.6 billion on a fully diluted basis, net of cash and marketable securities.

deals.explain: Cisco first agreed to pay $70 a share (about $2.6 billion) for Acacia, which makes the optical modules that send data over fiber between data centers. A long wait for Chinese regulatory approval led the two sides to renegotiate, and the price was raised in January 2021.

deals.title: Microsoft invests $1B in OpenAI

sources.quote: This $1 billion isn’t a lump-sum up-front investment — instead, it’s a total amount that can be delivered anytime over the next decade, in installments that correspond with funding efforts on OpenAI’s side that feed back into Microsoft’s own AI ambitions, as detailed by The New York Times.
The tech giant on Monday described its new agreement as the third stage of a growing partnership with San Francisco-based OpenAI that began with a $1 billion investment in 2019.

deals.explain: Microsoft put $1 billion into OpenAI in 2019, paid in stages, and OpenAI agreed to run its work on Microsoft's Azure cloud. This was the start of the partnership that made Microsoft OpenAI's biggest backer.

deals.title: Intel buys AI chip startup Habana Labs for about $2B

sources.quote: We acquired Habana Labs Ltd., an Israel-based developer of programmable deep learning accelerators for the data center, for approximately $1.7 billion.

deals.explain: Intel bought Israeli AI chip startup Habana Labs, maker of the Gaudi AI chips, in December 2019. It was announced as a roughly $2B deal; Intel's annual report puts the net price at about $1.7B, the amount shown.

deals.title: Nvidia's $40B bid for Arm (canceled 2022)

sources.quote: Under the terms of the transaction, which has been approved by the boards of directors of NVIDIA, SBG and Arm, NVIDIA will pay to SoftBank a total of $21.5 billion in NVIDIA common stock and $12 billion in cash, which includes $2 billion payable at signing.
The parties agreed to terminate the Purchase Agreement because of significant regulatory challenges preventing the consummation of the transaction.

deals.explain: Nvidia agreed to buy chip-design firm Arm from SoftBank for up to $40B in stock and cash (including a $5B performance earn-out and $1.5B of stock for Arm staff). Regulators in the US, UK and EU pushed back, and the deal was called off in February 2022; Nvidia wrote off a $1.25B prepayment.

deals.title: Energy Department gives TerraPower $80M to start Natrium reactor demo

sources.quote: DOE is awarding TerraPower LLC (Bellevue, Washington) and X-energy (Rockville, Maryland) $80 million each in initial funding to build two advanced nuclear reactors that can be operational within seven years.
The Department will invest a total of $3.2 billion over seven years, subject to the availability of future appropriations, with our industry partners providing matching funds.

deals.explain: The Energy Department granted TerraPower $80 million in first-year money to build a demonstration Natrium advanced reactor. DOE said it would put up to $3.2 billion over seven years into this and X-energy's project combined, depending on future budgets.

deals.title: Energy Department gives X-energy $80M to start Xe-100 reactor demo

sources.quote: DOE is awarding TerraPower LLC (Bellevue, Washington) and X-energy (Rockville, Maryland) $80 million each in initial funding to build two advanced nuclear reactors that can be operational within seven years.

deals.explain: The Energy Department granted X-energy $80 million in first-year money to build a demonstration of its Xe-100 small gas-cooled reactor, part of a program DOE said could total $3.2 billion over seven years for two projects.

deals.title: SK hynix buys Intel's NAND memory business for $9B

sources.quote: SK hynix will pay US $9 billion for the Intel NAND memory and storage business, which includes the NAND SSD business, the NAND component and wafer business, and the Dalian NAND memory manufacturing facility in China.
On March 27, 2025, we closed the second phase of the transaction.

deals.explain: SK hynix agreed to pay Intel $9 billion for its flash-memory (NAND) business, including a chip factory in Dalian, China. The deal closed in two steps: the first in December 2021 and the second in March 2025. Intel used the sale to exit memory and focus cash on its own chipmaking.

deals.title: AMD buys Xilinx in $35B all-stock deal

sources.quote: AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) and Xilinx (NASDAQ: XLNX) today announced they have entered into a definitive agreement for AMD to acquire Xilinx in an all-stock transaction valued at $35 billion.

deals.explain: AMD bought programmable-chip maker Xilinx, paying with AMD shares valued at $35B when announced; the deal closed in February 2022. It expanded AMD's data-center business ahead of its push into AI chips.

deals.title: Marvell buys Inphi for about $10B
